chunks: ‘Ali ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn Abī ‘Abdillāh al-Barqi, from al-Ḥasan ibn ‘Ali al-Washshā, who said:

I asked Imam al-Riḍā (peace be upon him): ‘What is the reward for one who visits the grave of your father, Abū al-Ḥasan (peace be upon him)?’ He replied: ‘Visit him.’ I asked: ‘What is among its merits?’ He said to him: ‘[It is] like that of one who visits the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him).’
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting the grave of Imam al-Kazim?
ai.summary: Imam al-Riḍā (peace be upon him) equates the spiritual reward of visiting the grave of Imam al-Kāẓim (peace be upon him) with that of Imam al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him), highlighting the profound status of the Imams as interconnected nodes of divine guidance. This comparison underscores the concept of *tawāṣul* (intercession) and the continuity of the Imamate, where the martyrdom and legacy of each Imam contribute to the collective spiritual merit of the Ahl al-Bayt. In Shia tradition, such equivalencies emphasize that the graves of the Imams serve as accessible portals for devotees to draw closer to God through the intercession of the Prophet’s household.
